headline: Open-Codemap v0.1.1 is on npm, everything it ships is verified, and the docs and release files are now accurate; no further work is planned yet.
overview: Open-Codemap helps AI coding tools find the right piece of code in a repository. It splits code into functions and classes, indexes them in one local SQLite file, and answers both exact-name and plain-English questions by combining meaning, keyword and code-structure search. It runs locally and can be used as a TypeScript library, a command-line tool or a small web API.

pillars.title: Structural indexing
pillars.body: Tree-sitter splits code into functions, classes and methods for about 150 languages.

pillars.title: Hybrid search
pillars.body: Meaning, exact names and the import/call graph are merged into one ranked list.

pillars.title: Local-first
pillars.body: One SQLite file per repo, no native build step, works offline with the mock embedder.

pillars.title: Three ways to use it
pillars.body: Library (ESM and CommonJS), CLI and HTTP API on the same engine.

sections.title: What works today
sections.body: Verified by running checks: parsing and chunking, incremental and live re-indexing, the SQLite store, all three embedders, hybrid retrieval, the CLI quickstart, the HTTP API, and the ESM + CommonJS build. All 100 tests pass and the published npm 0.1.1 matches the code. One command, pnpm check, runs lint, typecheck, build and tests locally.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.body: No retrieval-quality benchmark on real repositories yet, and large-repo performance is unknown. GitHub Actions is off on the account, so all checks run locally.

sections.title: Recent changes
sections.body: README now states the real default embedder (mock); the already-released changeset and a stale changelog line were removed; a pnpm check gate was added. All on the dev branch.

sections.title: Next up
sections.body: No milestone planned beyond housekeeping. Candidates: a retrieval-quality benchmark, a native sqlite-vec backend, a reranker, or a precise call graph.
